expected.summary: On the placed board: the autorouter passes route every open net and the planes are regenerated; each net reads back routed; the board is not saved.
Every net is routed already: nothing to route, the preview lists no change.
--layers must include the outer layers 1 and 4 of the 4-layer board; refused at the preview.
The session has no such board open.
A Designer and a Layout are both running (the usual state once the board exists), and the call names neither --session nor --doc: E_AMBIGUOUS lists both instances with their documents.

After placement, the person unplaces D1 in Layout: the nets of the placed parts are open and one component is unplaced, so the preview cannot apply, and the runtime refuses it as E_CONFLICT blocked, naming D1. (With every part unplaced Layout may report no open net; the preview then has nothing to do and the apply refuses with E_CONFLICT application_state.)
Run under a scope file that does not cover the target (the board's nets); nothing is previewed to the application's files or sent.

While a forward-annotation run or pcb export job of this tool runs in Layout, the session reports busy or unresponsive. Only --session is given: Layout does not say which board it has open while it does not answer, and a --doc it cannot match would be E_NOT_FOUND.

A person leaves a modal dialog open in Layout before the call, such as Setup > Setup Parameters or Help > About. Layout may go on answering COM, so a dialog box over it, or a Layout that stops answering, is reported as the session blocked with the dialog's title; E_HUMAN_REQUIRED with action dismiss_dialog and a resume command. Only --session is given, since a Layout that stops answering does not say which board it has open.
Layout goes away during a route pass; the nets stay locked until operation resolve.

rows.unrunnable: The COM connection to Layout cannot be cut on demand at the moment of a call; driver tests D06 and D21 cover how the runtime handles a lost connection.

expected.summary: The board holds unsaved changes (placement not yet saved): the router runs as usual; the receipt reports the document dirty.

The person draws a route obstruct over every layer around one pad of D1 first: the passes cannot connect that net, every pass still runs, and the net reads back routed false where the preview expected true.
